To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the primary sequence structure of a protein-coding DNA region can be modeled very well by a non-homogenous Markov process, and that the fit to observed amino acid usage is much better than for a spatially homogeneous model.

(1) the stochastic complexity of protein-coding regions can be reduced by 30% by allowing the Markov model to vary from codon to codon, (2) this non-homogeneous Markov model is a good fit to the observed codon preference in the protein data base, (3) the model is not a good fit to codon usage data in individual genes, (4) the model is a good predictor of codon usage in genes that are not represented in
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the phylogeny of species from DNA sequences.
the problem of finding the best model for a given sequence of symbols (codons) and the best model for the stochastic process which generates these sequences.
the stochastic complexity of a large data base of protein coding regions and the statistical properties of the primary sequence structure of the proteins they encode.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Markov model is not appropriate for the analysis of codon usage, at least not when the data base is large.
the primary sequence of protein-coding regions can be modeled with high precision as a non-homogenous Markov source, and that the non-homogeneity can be attributed to the codon preference.
the primary sequence structure of the data base is not well described by any of the models considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stochastic complexity of protein-coding regions can be explained by a non-homogenous Markov model with two parameters per site.
the primary sequence structure of protein-coding regions can be modeled as a Markov source with a non-homogenous transition matrix.
, when modeling the evolution of protein-coding regions, the Markov model is not good enough.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stochastic complexity of the primary sequence of a protein-coding region can be used to estimate the degree of non-homogeneity in the Markov source.
the stochastic complexity of a protein coding region is much larger when a spatially homogeneous model is used, and this has a significant influence on the estimation of substitution rates.
protein-coding DNA is highly structured and that this structure is not captured by a homogeneous Markov source.
